papers.summary: Spectral weight decay applies additive singular-value shrinkage. In 124M–500M LLaMA experiments, it improves low-rank compression at matched validation loss; the paper also reports gains under label noise.
papers.relevance: Direct match to spectral regularization, training for low-rank compressibility, and noisy-label generalization.

evidence.quote: Across LLaMA models with 124 124 M to 500 500 M parameters, spectral weight decay lowers effective rank and improves SVD-LLM compression at matched validation loss.

papers.title: Spectral Weight Decay: Inducing Low-Rank Structure in Neural Network Weights

papers.summary: BMuon changes Muon’s spectral geometry to encourage structured MLP-channel pruning. Its 1B language-model experiment reports substantially better pruning robustness, but worse unpruned perplexity than Muon.
papers.relevance: A direct test of whether optimizer geometry can make a trained model more compressible, with an important quality trade-off. Its compression is structured pruning, not low-rank factorization.

evidence.quote: On the unpruned models, Muon achieves lower perplexity ( 10.92 10.92 versus 12.84 12.84 for BMuon), but its performance degrades rapidly under pruning. In contrast, BMuon preserves its unpruned performance up to 80 % 80\% pruning, reaching 12.86 12.86 with activation ranking and 12.85 12.85 with μ \mu ranking.

papers.title: BMuon: Budgeting Muon's Spectral Geometry for Structured Compressibility

papers.summary: Analyzes how GD, simplified Adam, Muon, Shampoo, and K-FAC affect singular-mode emergence and decay in deep matrix factorization.
papers.relevance: Addresses how optimizer geometry changes spectral bias and effective rank, though the theory is not a direct LLM result.

evidence.quote: Under explicit balance and alignment assumptions, we derive birth, saturation, and decay laws for Euclidean GD, coordinate-wise updates of SignGD and an instantaneous Adam approximation, spectral updates of Muon and cumulative Shampoo, and a block curvature model of K-FAC.

papers.title: Optimizer Geometry Sets the Pace: Spectral Learning Dynamics in Matrix Factorization

papers.summary: Uses targeted orthogonalization and NanoGPT diagnostics to distinguish the effects of Muon on small momentum singular directions from its effects on weight spectra.
papers.relevance: Closely matches the interest in Muon, Newton–Schulz methods, and effective ranks of gradients, updates, and weights.

evidence.quote: Note that structure and performance don’t move together: AdamW collapses rank and still performs well, the bottom targeted variants keep Muon’s rank without matching its loss, and full-spectrum updates keep the spectrum flat for free.

papers.title: Spectrally Targeted Muon

papers.summary: Ori tracks drifting low-rank gradient subspaces during LLM pretraining. In its 1B LLaMA comparison, rank-32 optimizer-state peak memory is reported as 0.2487 GB versus 0.3385 GB for GaLore.
papers.relevance: Directly addresses low-rank gradients and memory-efficient pretraining. The quoted memory measure is optimizer state, not total peak GPU memory.

evidence.quote: For instance, at rank 32, Ori requires only 0.2487 GB, which is 12.1% less than OSD (0.2832 GB) and 26.5% less than GaLore (0.3385 GB).

papers.title: Ori: Drift-Aware Streaming $k$-PCA for Very Low-Rank LLM Training

papers.summary: Clean uses Nyström sketches for curvature-aware LLM pretraining; Q-Clean further compresses optimizer states. At 1.3B parameters, the reported trade-offs differ: Clean has lower final perplexity, while Q-Clean has lower peak memory.
papers.relevance: Provides measured quality, optimizer-state, total-memory, and wall-clock comparisons for memory-efficient pretraining.

papers.title: Clean: Second-order LLM Training at Linear Memory Cost via Nystr{ö}m Sketching

papers.summary: Monarch–Muon applies matrix-aware optimization to structured weights. The paper reports quality comparisons at smaller scales and separate 6.89B systems measurements of memory and step time.
papers.relevance: Connects parameterization and Muon to model-quality, training-memory, and throughput trade-offs across scales.

evidence.quote: In quality runs, Monarch–Muon improves over Monarch–AdamW at fixed structure: 3.06 vs. 3.09 in the dense 257M model and 2.68 vs. 2.77 in the 1B MoE model; the two-block MoE variant also matches dense AdamW while using 15% fewer active and 25.4% fewer total parameters. In 6.89B-parameter systems measurements, Monarch–Muon reduces peak memory from 68.9 to 52.9 GB, Muon optimizer state from 14.60 to 6.77 GB, and the Muon optimizer step from 1288 to 304 ms.

papers.title: Monarch-Muon: Structure-Aware Muon for Fast and Memory-Efficient Pretraining

papers.summary: Module-matched LoRA rank sweeps compare adapters with dense fine-tuning under label noise. In the 7B language-model experiment, every sampled adapter rank remains behind dense fine-tuning on test NLL.
papers.relevance: Directly links LoRA rank and parameter efficiency to memorization and generalization under noisy labels.

evidence.quote: The 7 7 B rank axis is the clearest case for reading the tail against a module-matched baseline rather than against the pre-peak valley. Every sampled rank, parity included, remains behind dense in all three seeds

papers.title: LoRA's Second Descent Extends Beyond Parameter Parity

papers.summary: Studies how finite-rank observation bottlenecks and trace-norm regularization constrain the rank of LoRA solutions without relying on network linearization.
papers.relevance: Addresses LoRA rank selection and nuclear-norm regularization, both central to the profile.

evidence.quote: Trace-norm regularization then forces the optimizer to pick a low-rank matrix among all matrices that produce the same observed output.

papers.title: How Finite-Rank Bottlenecks Shape the Low-Rank Adaptation Landscape

papers.summary: Idea2Prior combines candidate discovery, identity checks, abstract assessment, citation expansion, and evidence-backed ranking for idea-to-paper retrieval. Its historical comparison reports 16/30 target hits, with a harder-query exception.
papers.relevance: Directly informs a research-digest harness’s paper retrieval, relevance ranking, and evidence auditability.

evidence.quote: The reported aggregate Hit@5 is 16/30 for Idea2Prior, 13/30 for ChatGPT web Deep Research, and 11/30 for Gemini web Deep Research.
Idea2Prior leads both baselines by 20 percentage points on EASY and MEDIUM, but trails ChatGPT by 10 points on HARD.

papers.title: Idea2Prior: Auditable Paper Retrieval and Ranking from Research Ideas

limitations: These are reported paper results, not independent replications; repository availability was not verified as evidence of reproducibility.
Ori’s cited memory comparison measures optimizer-state peak memory, not total training memory.
BMuon’s reported compression uses structured channel pruning and trades away unpruned language-model quality.
The matrix-factorization theory may not transfer directly to LLM weight spectra. Idea2Prior’s historical comparison uses a small, overlapping target set.
